[ERROR LIST]
- Line 85: `pendingPayload` is read and cleared under `lock`, but the comment claiming it is “written from WKScriptMessageHandler queue, read from display link” is not enforced by the type or API; `delegate?.layoutEngine(_:didReceive:)` still receives every decoded payload immediately, while `consumePendingPayload()` may consume only the latest one. This creates inconsistent delivery semantics: intermediate payloads can be delivered to the delegate but never be available to the consumer.
- Line 88: `frameCache` is declared and invalidated but is never read or populated anywhere in the supplied code. The stated “skip redundant delegate calls” behavior is unimplemented.
- Line 98: `invalidateCache()` acquires `lock` for `frameCache`, but no other access to `frameCache` exists. The cache has no functional effect.
- Line 125: The direct-`Data` fallback is effectively redundant for normal WebKit JavaScript messages: JavaScript values delivered by `WKScriptMessage.body` are bridged property-list-compatible Foundation values, while arbitrary native `Data` is not a normal JavaScript message payload type. This is not a runtime failure, but it is dead handling for the stated JavaScript bridge use case.[1][2]
- Line 156: `decoder` is a shared mutable class instance accessed without synchronization. If `userContentController(_:didReceive:)` is invoked concurrently, concurrent calls to `decoder.decode` are not guaranteed safe because `JSONDecoder` is not `Sendable` and should not be assumed safe across concurrent tasks/threads.[3]
- Line 161: The delegate callback occurs on the message-handler execution context rather than being dispatched to the main thread. A delegate that updates UIKit or other main-thread-confined state can therefore cause main-thread violations or crashes. Only error callbacks are explicitly dispatched to the main queue.
- Line 161: The callback is invoked after releasing `lock`, so a second message can overwrite `pendingPayload` before the delegate processes the first payload. The delegate is told that payload A was received even though `consumePendingPayload()` can return payload B.
- Line 161: A retained `LayoutBridge` can call its weak delegate synchronously from an arbitrary callback context. Since `delegate` is neither synchronized nor main-actor isolated, concurrent assignment/removal of the delegate can race with this access.
- Line 37: `hasTransform` returns `true` when only `transformA` is present, although `affineTransform` returns `.identity` unless all six matrix components are non-`nil`. A partially supplied transform is therefore reported as present but resolves to no transform.
- Line 52: `resolvedColor` passes component values directly to `UIColor`. Unlike `resolvedOpacity`, it does not clamp values to the required 0...1 range. Decoded color components outside that range can produce invalid/unintended colors rather than a normalized result.
- Line 59: `devicePixelRatio` is decoded but never applied to frames, dimensions, transforms, borders, fonts, padding, or scroll positions. If payload geometry is expressed in device pixels rather than UIKit points, every rendered measurement is scaled incorrectly.
- Line 60: `scrollY` in `LayoutPayload` is decoded but unused.
- Lines 17 and 32: `scrollY` exists both per element and at payload level, but neither value is applied to `frame`; element coordinates are therefore not adjusted for scrolling by this code.
- Lines 11-34: All geometric, opacity, z-index, transform, font, padding, and color values accept `Double.nan` and infinities if they originate from a non-JSON `Codable` decoder source, but this bridge uses JSON where non-finite numeric values are invalid. No validation rejects negative sizes, invalid radii, non-finite values, or malformed layout geometry after decoding.
- Lines 71-72: The delegate protocol exposes `LayoutBridge` publicly, but `LayoutBridge` does not expose any rendering, frame-cache lookup, element comparison, or application API. The declared layout-engine interface does not implement the advertised cache-based layout behavior.
- Lines 193-195: `WeakScriptMessageHandler` holds its delegate weakly. If the caller registers `WeakScriptMessageHandler(delegate: LayoutBridge())` without separately strongly retaining that `LayoutBridge`, the bridge is immediately deallocated and all JavaScript messages are silently discarded.
- Lines 185-200: `WeakScriptMessageHandler` only avoids the retain cycle if the actual delegate is retained elsewhere. The file provides no ownership mechanism or registration/removal lifecycle, so normal use can either silently lose message delivery through delegate deallocation or leave the wrapper registered indefinitely.
[END OF LIST]

[ERROR LIST]
- Line 10: `blitPipelineState` requires Metal functions named `vertexPassthrough` and `fragmentWebGLBlit`, but this file neither supplies a `.metal` source file nor verifies that those functions exist. If either function is absent from the app’s default Metal library, pipeline creation cannot succeed and no source texture is rendered.
- Line 14: `preferredFramesPerSecond120` is never read after initialization. It has no effect on frame rate selection.
- Line 22: `fatalError` terminates the process on a device without Metal support rather than allowing the caller to handle initialization failure.
- Lines 31-35: Frame rate selection is based solely on the iOS 15 availability check. iOS 15 support does not guarantee a 120 Hz display; assigning 120 on a 60 Hz display does not create 120 Hz rendering and ignores the unused `preferredFramesPerSecond120` setting.
- Line 35: `preferredFramesPerSecond` does not guarantee that `draw(_:)` is invoked at 120 Hz; actual presentation cadence is determined by display capability and system scheduling.
- Lines 42-44: If `device.makeCommandQueue()` returns `nil`, initialization continues without reporting failure. Every future `draw(_:)` invocation returns without rendering.
- Line 46: If `makeDefaultLibrary()` returns `nil`, `setupMetal` returns silently. `commandQueue` may exist, but `blitPipelineState` and `samplerState` remain unusable, so the view cannot render source textures.
- Lines 48-49: `makeFunction(name:)` can return `nil`, but the code does not validate either function before building the pipeline descriptor. Pipeline creation then fails later with a less direct error.
- Lines 53-62: The pipeline’s target pixel format is hard-coded to `.bgra8Unorm` instead of using `colorPixelFormat`. If `colorPixelFormat` is changed after initialization, the render pipeline and drawable pixel formats can differ, causing render-pipeline validation failure or rendering failure.
- Lines 66-70: Pipeline creation failure is only printed. The view remains active and repeatedly enters the rendering path with a `nil` pipeline state.
- Lines 79-85: The layer search is limited to 60 calls, not to a reliable lifecycle event. If the `WKWebView` backing layer hierarchy does not yet contain a `CAMetalLayer` during those calls, subsequent attempts permanently stop even if the hierarchy later changes.
- Lines 79-85: Searching the `WKWebView`’s Core Animation subtree for an arbitrary `CAMetalLayer` does not establish that the discovered layer contains WebGL content. A `WKWebView` implementation detail may contain no `CAMetalLayer`, may contain multiple such layers, or may change layers during navigation, process replacement, resizing, backgrounding, or WebKit updates.
- Lines 87-96: `findCAMetalLayer(in:)` recursively traverses the entire layer subtree with no cycle protection. Although normal Core Animation layer trees are acyclic, this method assumes that invariant and can recurse indefinitely if a malformed layer graph is supplied.
- Line 99: `injectWebGLTexture(_:)` merely stores an externally supplied texture. It neither validates texture compatibility with this view’s device nor synchronizes access with `draw(_:)`.
- Line 100: `lastKnownTexture` may be a texture created by a different `MTLDevice` from the view’s device. Binding it to an encoder created by this view’s command queue is invalid and causes a Metal validation error or undefined rendering behavior.
- Line 100: `lastKnownTexture` retains the most recently supplied texture indefinitely. If producers continuously provide new textures, the view retains one old texture until replacement or deallocation; if the producer expects a drawable-backed texture to be released promptly, this retention can keep drawable resources occupied.
- Lines 102-143: `draw(_:)` accesses and mutates `webGLSourceLayer`, `lastKnownTexture`, `layerSearchAttempts`, `commandQueue`, `blitPipelineState`, and `samplerState` without enforcing main-thread execution or serial synchronization. Calling public methods from another thread while MetalKit draws can create data races.
- Lines 104-106: The view acquires `currentDrawable` and `currentRenderPassDescriptor` before determining whether a usable source texture and a valid pipeline are available. This unnecessarily holds the drawable while source discovery and setup checks occur, increasing drawable-pool pressure. Apple recommends acquiring drawables as late as possible.[1]
- Lines 111-113: When `lastKnownTexture` is absent, the code calls `extractTextureFromCAMetalLayer`, but that method does not read from the source layer’s current drawable or any WebKit-rendered texture. The returned texture is newly allocated and contains undefined/uninitialized image data.
- Lines 116-124: The no-source-texture branch creates a render encoder only to end it after configuring a clear load action. Although this may clear the drawable, it does not set `storeAction`; it relies on the descriptor’s preexisting value rather than explicitly specifying the intended result.
- Lines 116-124: The no-source-texture branch presents a cleared frame on every scheduled draw. Once a valid frame was previously displayed, a transient missing source texture causes the view to flash transparent rather than preserving the previous valid image.
- Lines 130-134: If a render encoder is created but either `blitPipelineState` or `samplerState` is `nil`, the `guard` fails after encoder creation. The encoder is never ended, yet the command buffer is presented and committed. This produces an invalid command buffer because Metal requires an active encoder to be ended before commit.
- Lines 130-134: In the same failure branch, the drawable is presented without a completed render pass. The result is undefined/cleared/previous drawable content depending on implementation rather than a deliberate output.
- Lines 137-140: The draw call assumes `vertexPassthrough` supplies all required vertex data without any bound vertex buffer or vertex descriptor. If the vertex shader expects vertex attributes or buffers, the draw produces validation errors or invalid geometry.
- Lines 138-139: The code samples `texture` without checking that its `pixelFormat` is sampleable by the fragment shader, that it is compatible with the shader’s declared texture type, that it has `.shaderRead` usage, or that it belongs to the same `MTLDevice`.
- Lines 137-140: The code performs no texture-coordinate transformation, origin conversion, scaling correction, viewport correction, or synchronization with WebKit rendering. Even with a valid injected texture, source orientation and dimensions can be wrong.
- Lines 146-177: `extractTextureFromCAMetalLayer(_:)` does not extract a texture from `metalLayer`. It reads only `drawableSize` and `pixelFormat`, allocates a separate texture, and returns it without copying any source pixels. `CAMetalLayer` exposes drawable textures through `nextDrawable()`, not through layer metadata.[2][3]
- Line 148: The method uses `self.device` rather than verifying that `metalLayer.device` is non-`nil` and identical to the view’s device. A source layer associated with another device cannot be copied or sampled by this view’s command queue.
- Lines 149-151: `drawableSize` is not evidence that a renderable WebGL frame exists. A nonzero size only permits allocation of a blank destination texture.
- Lines 153-158: The newly created texture descriptor copies the source layer’s pixel format without checking whether the format is valid for shader sampling, render targeting, or compatible with the fragment shader.
- Line 159: `.shared` storage mode is explicitly selected for an off-screen texture even though the CPU never accesses the texture. This is unnecessary and can be less appropriate than device-private storage for GPU-only resources; it is not a mechanism for accessing another layer’s drawable.
- Lines 163-174: The command buffer and blit encoder created here do not encode any blit command. The `region` is created and discarded, then an empty blit encoder is committed. No bytes are copied from any source texture to `texture`.
- Lines 167-171: `region` is dead code. It is calculated but never supplied to a Metal command.
- Lines 166-174: The code commits an empty command buffer asynchronously and immediately returns `texture`. The caller can sample the returned texture before the empty command buffer completes; more importantly, no rendering or transfer ever initializes it.
- Line 176: The returned texture has undefined contents because it was allocated but never cleared, rendered into, or copied into. Rendering it can show arbitrary memory contents, stale GPU data, or visual corruption.
- Lines 179-183: `updateSourceWebView(_:)` resets only the located layer and retry counter. It does not clear `lastKnownTexture`, so content from the old web view can continue being displayed after the source web view changes.
- Lines 179-183: `updateSourceWebView(_:)` does not trigger a redraw. With `enableSetNeedsDisplay = false`, replacing the source may not be visible until MetalKit schedules another draw.
- Lines 79-85 and 179-183: The code has no observation mechanism for the source `WKWebView`’s layer creation, destruction, resizing, navigation, or process changes. A cached `CAMetalLayer` can become stale and the view will continue attempting to use it.
- Lines 10, 48-49, and 137-140: This file depends on external shader functions but contains no shader implementation. As provided, it is not a complete compilable rendering feature unless a correctly configured default Metal library exists elsewhere.
[END OF LIST]
that's all.
